messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING @laura (oncall) — prod-east streaming p99 surge detected on /v1/generate/stream. Runbook auto-started.

laura: ack. looking at dashboards. how many regions impacted?

dan: only prod-east showing spike. p95 jumped 0.9s->1.9s, p99 2.7s->7.4s starting ~2479001042. spikes correlate with node gpu-7c telemetry: repeated memory-correctable ECC, nvlink resets.

jyoti: grabbing node telemetry now. BMC and iDRAC show fan_tach lower on slot 7 and a transient PSU current drop. excerpts:
```
[2479001039] hwmon: sensor fan7_tach = 1200 RPM (expected 4200)
[2479001041] ipmi: PSU1 current drop: 11.2A -> 7.9A
[2479001042] nvidia: GPU 0000:7c:00.0: Correctable ECC errors: 42
[2479001043] nvlink: peer reset on GPU 7c -> link flapping
```

marco: hypothesis: card hitting thermal/airflow margin and NVLink resets cause kernel fallback to safe path -> token generation stalls and streaming tail spikes. mitigation: 1) switch affected traffic to int8-quantized variant (lower perf/quality tradeoff but less memory pressure) 2) cordon gpu-7c and migrate sessions 3) throttle non-critical customers and enable shed for background batch jobs.

ops-bot: commands queued: `cordon-node gpu-7c`, `migrate-sessions --node=gpu-7c --strategy=stream-migrate --grace=90s`, `autoscale cpu-fallback +3`. Executing...

ops-bot: cordon complete. migration started. in-flight session migration will attempt TCP handover; streaming clients may see transient resets.

dan: applying routing fallback: route rule added -> prefer [gpu-8a, gpu-8b] then cpu-fallback; model-family fallback -> gptx-qa-int8 as first preference for prod-east streaming. Applied at 2479001105.

jyoti: live kernel logs show runtime switching to slow attention kernel on gpu-7c prior to NVLink resets. That explains latency cliff when certain kernel paths are chosen.

marco: lowering streaming window/batch window to reduce scheduling latency: `runtime-config set streaming.batch_window_ms 12` for prod-east. Also toggled `runtime:prefer_small_kernels=true` for affected routes.

dan: initial results: p99 dropped from 7.4s -> 3.2s within 45s of migration. Still see elevated tail for long-context (>64k token) sessions due to KV checkpoint misses.

ops-bot: cpu-fallback scaled. traffic shifted: ~78% to gpu-8a/8b, 15% cpu-fallback, 7% still draining on gpu-7c.

jyoti: manual KV prewarm started for top prefixes (script: `kv-prewarm --customers-file /tmp/top_prefixes.txt --targets gpu-8a,gpu-8b`) to reduce rewarm stalls.

cs-team: customer impact summary: 5 customers with >25% p99 degradation; 2 customers reported stream resets, 1 filed a Support ticket (INC-4723). CS sent initial notification and mitigation ETA 20m.

infra-team: hardware ops notified. Recommended immediate replacement of GPU module in slot 7 and verifying rack airflow (fan assembly replacement if tach doesn't recover). Planning maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

marco: for postmortem: capture runtime kernel selection traces and evaluate graceful degrade behavior under NVLink flapping. Also consider adding per-node NVLink/correctable-ECC anomaly alerts and a fan-tach low RPM alert.

laura: handoff: I'll watch metrics for 15 more minutes, then hand to @dan for post-incident. Action items: 1) hw replacement (owner infra-team) 2) postmortem (owner dan) 3) add alerting thresholds + routing test in staging.

dan: taking postmortem ownership. I'll collect logs (nvml, nvlink, dmesg, bmc dumps, routing rules) and start RCA doc in #postmortems. timeline and initial RCA draft in 12h.

ops-bot: migration complete. gpu-7c status: CORDONED -> DRAINED. No further sessions on node.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: Sev2. postmortem owner: dan.

laura: thanks everyone for quick response. noted follow-ups: improve session migration resiliency for streaming (TCP handover fallback), and prewarm KV during heavy model switching. :thumbsup:
